world.title: Zookeeper Mauled By Leopard In Zoo Enclosure In Netherlands, Fighting For Life
world.summary: A zookeeper is in critical condition after being mauled by a leopard at Beekse Bergen Safari Park in the Netherlands. The incident occurred on Saturday morning, resulting in severe head injuries. The victim was airlifted to a local hospital, where she is receiving treatment, including surgery. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack.

world.title: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
world.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has faced criticism from economists and political opponents for proposing the use of cryptocurrency to circumvent economic sanctions. His comments prompted a rare rebuke from the Bank of Israel. Netanyahu is currently seeking re-election, and the suggestion has raised concerns about its implications for the Israeli economy and regulatory framework surrounding digital currencies.

world.title: ‘A defeat for the Republic’: How October 17 protest fiasco shaped France’s security strategy
world.summary: On October 24, France mobilized 70,000 security personnel nationwide, supported by elite police units, helicopters, drones, and armored vehicles, following a significant protest on October 17, which drew an estimated 550,000 participants. This response reflects a shift in France's security strategy, emphasizing heightened preparedness and resource allocation to manage large-scale demonstrations and maintain public order.

business.title: TVS Sales Breakup Sep 2026 - Jupiter, Apache, XL, iQube, Raider, Ntorq, Radeon
business.summary: TVS Motor Company reported a 16.65% increase in domestic two-wheeler sales, reaching 4.82 lakh units in September 2026. Exports also saw significant growth, rising by 29.74% to 1.57 lakh units. The company experienced positive performance in both domestic and international markets during this period, reflecting strong demand for its range of two-wheeler models.

business.title: IndiGo, Air India Group To Shift Flights To Navi Mumbai Airport
business.summary: IndiGo and the Air India Group will gradually transfer selected domestic and international flights from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport to Navi Mumbai International Airport. Air India Express plans to initiate four daily domestic flights from NMIA in December 2026, with a phased transition of its West Asia operations starting in January 2027.

business.title: RailTel Interim Dividend 2026: Navratna PSU announces payout alongside Q2 results; Check record date
business.summary: RailTel Corporation of India announced an interim dividend alongside its Q2 results. For the quarter ending September 30, 2026, total income rose to Rs 1,149.06 crore, up from Rs 965.74 crore year-on-year. However, consolidated net profit decreased by 9.9% to Rs 68.56 crore, while total expenses increased to Rs 1,024.59 crore from Rs 844.31 crore.

technology.title: iPhone Duo owners report screens cracking days after unboxing, flag possible hinge defect
technology.summary: iPhone Duo owners have reported inner screens cracking along the hinge just days after unboxing, raising concerns about a potential hardware defect. The scale and cause of the issue are still unclear. Additionally, some reviewers noted that several applications were not properly optimized for the foldable design, suggesting that Apple may need to address app compatibility.

technology.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
technology.summary: State attorneys general are addressing the issue of excessive filters in selfies posted by teens on social media, following a recent settlement with Meta. The agreement includes a clause prohibiting "cosmetic procedure filters" for minors. However, defining what constitutes an extreme makeover remains challenging, raising concerns about the impact of filtered images on youth self-image and mental health.

technology.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
technology.summary: State attorneys general are addressing the issue of excessive filters in selfies posted by teens on social media following a recent settlement with Meta. The agreement prohibits "cosmetic procedure filters" for minors, but defining what constitutes an extreme makeover remains challenging. This raises concerns about the impact of such filters on youth self-image and online behavior.

sports.title: Shaheen Afridi Overtakes Waqar Younis, Shoaib Akhtar To Set New Pakistan ODI Record
sports.summary: Pakistan ODI captain Shaheen Afridi set a new record by becoming the fastest bowler to reach 150 wickets in One Day Internationals. This achievement occurred during the second match of the ODI tri-series against England at Gaddafi Stadium. Afridi surpassed former Pakistani bowlers Waqar Younis and Shoaib Akhtar, marking a significant milestone in his cricketing career.

sports.title: Anderson to leave Lancashire after 25 years, but no retirement yet
sports.summary: James Anderson will leave Lancashire after 25 years, as the club has declined to offer him a new contract. The England cricket legend expressed disappointment, stating that if it were up to him, the situation would not have concluded this way. Despite his departure from Lancashire, Anderson has not announced plans for retirement from cricket.

sports.title: Lancashire end 25-year association with James Anderson
sports.summary: James Anderson, 44, confirmed via Instagram that he will no longer play for Lancashire, ending a 25-year association with the county. Lancashire decided not to extend his contract, and Anderson stated that the decision was not his own. He did not indicate any plans for retirement in his announcement, leaving his future in cricket open-ended.

health.title: AI can help doctors detect TB and lung cancer earlier: Dr Randeep Guleria
health.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) may significantly enhance India's efforts to combat tuberculosis (TB) and lung cancer, according to experts. AI can facilitate earlier detection, expedite diagnosis, and improve patient screening processes. This technological advancement aims to transform healthcare outcomes for these diseases, potentially leading to better management and treatment options for patients in India, as highlighted by Dr. Randeep Guleria.

health.title: World Stroke Day 2026: How to recognise a stroke and what to do immediately
health.summary: World Stroke Day, observed on October 29, emphasizes the importance of early stroke recognition and prompt medical attention. Quick action can save brain cells, prevent disability, and save lives. Symptoms may include sudden inability to speak clearly or other neurological signs. Timely intervention is crucial, as many strokes are treatable and preventable with the right response.

health.title: Fatty liver is not just about alcohol: Gastroenterologist explains the role of diabetes, belly fat and cholesterol
health.summary: Fatty liver disease can affect non-drinkers and often remains undetected. A gastroenterologist highlights that diabetes, excess belly fat, high cholesterol, and insulin resistance contribute to its development. Warning signs may be subtle, making awareness crucial. Protecting liver health involves lifestyle changes and monitoring these risk factors, emphasizing that fatty liver is not solely linked to alcohol consumption.

science.title: Stars from 'The Three-Body Problem' are real after all
science.summary: Chinese astronomers have discovered a stable three-star system, differing from the chaotic portrayal in Liu Cixin's _The Three-Body Problem_. The system includes a pulsar spinning over 300 times per second and a white dwarf, with the pulsar orbiting the white dwarf every eight days. A Sun-like star orbits the pair, completing its orbit in 73.5 years.

science.title: Nearly 300 glaciers lost in US since the 1960s: Study
science.summary: A study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences reveals that nearly 300 glaciers have disappeared in the western United States since the 1960s. Utilizing satellite data and aerial photography, researchers tracked glacier retreat across six states. The findings indicate that smaller, south-facing glaciers at lower elevations are particularly vulnerable to climate change effects.

science.title: Does Mars have 2 potato-shaped Moons? Japan’s MMX Mission 2026 may solve the rare mystery
science.summary: Mars has two irregularly shaped moons, Phobos and Deimos, whose origins are still uncertain. Japan’s MMX mission, set to launch in 2026, aims to determine whether these moons are captured asteroids or formed from debris resulting from a giant impact. The investigation may provide insights into the moons' formation and the history of the Martian system.

entertainment.title: Satish Kaushik's Lookalike Leaves Anil Kapoor Nostalgic, Actor Recalls Their Bond On India Ke Top 1%
entertainment.summary: Anil Kapoor reminisced about his late friend, actor-filmmaker Satish Kaushik, during an episode of India Ke Top 1%. This nostalgia was triggered by a contestant who bore a striking resemblance to Kaushik, who passed away on March 9, 2023, at the age of 66. Kapoor reflected on their bond, sharing heartfelt memories during the show.

entertainment.title: Javed Akhtar defends Rashmika Mandanna amid criticism over her Hindi accent; says, 'This fake and baseless linguistic superiority is not acceptable'
entertainment.summary: Javed Akhtar has defended actor Rashmika Mandanna following criticism of her Hindi accent. The veteran lyricist expressed his disapproval of the notion of linguistic superiority, labeling it as "fake and baseless." Akhtar's comments came after Mandanna addressed the backlash regarding her pronunciation in Hindi films, emphasizing the need for acceptance and support in the entertainment industry.

entertainment.title: Rise And Fall 2's Sara Gurpal Reveals She Received Death And Rape Threats After Eviction
entertainment.summary: Sara Gurpal, following her eviction from Rise And Fall 2, reported receiving death and rape threats online. She condemned the harassment, stating that while differing opinions are acceptable, targeting her and her family with such threats and making vulgar comments about her body is unacceptable. The singer-actor emphasized the need for respectful discourse amid the backlash she faced.
